title: Knowledge Graph RAG explained in 5min
description:
Understanding Knowledge Graph RAG: Elevating Retrieval-Augmented Generation

In this video, we dive into Knowledge Graph RAG and compare it with vector database RAG for retrieval-augmented generation. We explore how vector DB RAG works by chunking a document into smaller pieces and creating semantic embeddings for each chunk, which are then used for search queries through cosine similarity. However, this approach lacks relational context between chunks. Conversely, Knowledge Graph RAG maintains these relationships, connecting chunks, books, and other entities like authors through nodes and edges in a graph. This method enhances retrieval capabilities, making it particularly useful for complex data relationships and is utilized by major search engines like Google and Bing.

title: Protein Hydrolysis and Cleavage Overview | Bioanalytics
description:
Breaking Down Proteins: Hydrolysis and Cleavage Explained

In this episode, we delve into protein analysis by exploring two main methods: protein hydrolysis and protein cleavage. We cover how protein hydrolysis uses acid, base, or enzymatic processes to break down proteins into individual amino acids. The episode also details protein cleavage, focusing on breaking proteins at specific sites to create peptides. Techniques such as ion exchange and RP-HPLC chromatography for filtering amino acids, as well as endoprotease and chemical cleavage methods for peptide analysis, are discussed. This comprehensive guide aids in understanding the processes used to analyze protein structures in biochemical research.

title: Protein Separation (Electrophoresis and SDS PAGE) | Bioanalytics
description:
Understanding Electrophoresis and SDS PAGE in Protein and DNA Separation

In this video, we delve into the process of separating proteins and DNA using electrophoresis. The host explains the basic principles of electrophoresis, describing how a gel matrix and an electric current are used to separate molecules by size. The video also covers SDS PAGE, a technique that allows the separation of proteins by making them uniformly negatively charged. Additional methods such as the use of a stacking gel, resolving gel, and beta-mercaptoethanol for breaking disulfide bonds between protein molecules are discussed. Finally, the host explains how a molecular weight ladder is used to estimate the size of separated proteins. This comprehensive guide is ideal for students and researchers looking to understand the principles behind these crucial biochemical techniques.

title: Protein Purification Basics (Clearly explained) | Bioanalytics
description:
Protein Purification Made Simple: Step-by-Step Guide for Beginners

In this episode, we delve into the process of protein purification, explained in an easy-to-understand manner, ideal for those without a biology background. The video covers the four main steps: cell and tissue disruption, centrifugation, salting out, and desalting. It elaborates on gentle, harsh, and cryo grinding methods for cell disruption, followed by a detailed explanation of centrifugation to separate organelles and proteins. The process of salting out proteins and removing the salt using dialysis, ultrafiltration, or gel filtration is also discussed. Additionally, insights on using pH buffers, detergents, and protease inhibitors to maintain protein integrity are provided. Join us to learn the fundamentals of protein purification efficiently!

title: How beginner level research in AI and ML looks like
description:
In this video, I share my thesis presentation on novel methods for comparing audio and text for retrieval. I delve into the limitations of traditional search engines and propose a new approach to search through multiple modalities without relying on text comparison. By converting text and audio into vectors called embeddings and calculating their similarity, we aim to improve accuracy. I discuss the baseline system, our proposed method of transforming embeddings into pseudo-images for a vision transformer, and our experimental results. Despite underwhelming performance, this exploration offers valuable insights and potential future improvements. Special thanks to my team members and supervisors for their support.
